## What to remember {#revision-essentials}

- For target q and prediction p, cross-entropy H(q,p) is the average of −log p(x) weighted by q(x).
- It equals H(q) + D_KL(q ∥ p). With q fixed, it is minimized when p matches q.
- If the target is concentrated on observed token y, it becomes −log p(y). Predictive entropy H(p) addresses uncertainty before observing the outcome.
- In a GPT, the output at position i is compared with target i + 1. The loss mask excludes invalid targets. The causal mask limits the positions visible when computing the prediction.

## Recall from memory {#revision-check}

With target token y, why can you redistribute the remaining mass without changing its penalty when p(y) stays fixed?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

A one-hot target gives weight only to y’s term. The penalty is −log p(y) regardless of how the rest is distributed.

</details>
